phones_sentence: Service office phones, addresses and hours come from the New Jersey Department of Veterans Affairs Veterans Service Offices page. Call before you go.

programs.name: New Jersey veterans: state service officers for claims help
programs.organization: New Jersey Department of Veterans Affairs, Veterans Service Offices
programs.description: Free help from the New Jersey Department of Veterans Affairs’ accredited Veterans Service Officers with VA claims, appeals, pension and survivor benefits, plus state veterans benefits. The department runs a Veterans Service Office in every county.
programs.next_step: Choose your county for its service office, or call 844-671-1019 to be connected to the office for your county. For questions about state veterans benefits, call the NJ Veterans Benefits Hotline at 888-865-8387.
constraints: Most offices close on alternate Fridays, and a few keep shorter hours; call before you go.

programs.name: New Jersey Aging and Disability Resource Connection
programs.organization: New Jersey Department of Human Services, Division of Aging Services
programs.description: New Jersey’s statewide aging line. It connects older adults, people with disabilities and caregivers to the county office on aging for information, meals, in-home help, transportation and caregiver support. Military service is not required.
programs.next_step: Call 877-222-3737, or choose a county above for its office on aging.
constraints: Each program has its own eligibility and waitlist.
Give your county so the call reaches the right office.

programs.name: Medicare counseling (SHIP) for New Jersey
programs.organization: New Jersey Department of Human Services, State Health Insurance Assistance Program
programs.description: Free, unbiased help from trained SHIP counselors with Medicare choices, claims, Medigap, Medicare Advantage, Part D and help paying Medicare costs. Counseling sites operate in all 21 counties.
programs.next_step: Call the SHIP line at 800-792-8820, or call your county office on aging to set up an appointment. For Medicare itself, call 800-MEDICARE (800-633-4227).
constraints: Counselors do not sell or recommend plans. Have your Medicare card and drug list ready.

programs.name: New Jersey Long-Term Care Ombudsman and adult abuse reporting
programs.organization: New Jersey Office of the Long-Term Care Ombudsman
programs.description: Advocacy for residents of nursing homes, assisted living and other long-term care facilities. The office investigates complaints about care, rights, abuse, neglect and exploitation, and callers may stay anonymous.
programs.next_step: Call 877-582-6995 and press option 1, or email ombudsman@ltco.nj.gov. To report suspected abuse, neglect or exploitation of an adult living in the community, call Adult Protective Services at 855-TELL-APS (855-835-5277). In an emergency, call 911.
constraints: The ombudsman is not a first responder or a licensing agency; complaints about licensed facilities can also go to the New Jersey Department of Health at 800-792-9770.

programs.name: Free legal help for New Jersey veterans and older adults
programs.organization: Legal Services of New Jersey; Volunteer Lawyers for Justice Veterans Legal Program
programs.description: Legal Services of New Jersey runs the statewide LSNJLAW Hotline, which gives free civil legal advice and referrals to low-income residents in all 21 counties, with special programs for older adults. Volunteer Lawyers for Justice’s Veterans Legal Program gives free civil legal help to veterans across the state.
programs.next_step: Call the LSNJLAW Hotline at 888-576-5529 (Monday–Friday, 8:00 a.m.–5:30 p.m.) or apply online. Veterans can also call Volunteer Lawyers for Justice at 973-645-1955.
constraints: Legal Services handles civil, non-criminal matters and screens by income.
Volunteer programs cannot promise a lawyer for every case.

programs.name: VA health care systems serving New Jersey
programs.description: Most New Jersey veterans are served by the VA New Jersey Health Care System (East Orange VA Medical Center, 385 Tremont Avenue, 973-676-1000; Lyons VA Medical Center, 151 Knollcroft Road, 908-647-0180) and its clinics. South Jersey is also served by the Philadelphia VA Medical Center (215-823-5800) and the Wilmington VA Medical Center (302-994-2511 or 800-461-8262), which runs clinics in Atlantic, Cape May and Cumberland counties.
programs.next_step: Use VA’s facility locator with your ZIP code to find the closest clinic and its medical center. Not enrolled yet? Ask your county’s Veterans Service Office for help applying.
constraints: Which system serves you depends on where you live; VA’s locator shows the right clinic.

County offices on aging come from the Division of Aging Services list; Centers for Independent Living from the Division of Disability Services list, checked against the ILRU national directory. The ombudsman is a single statewide office.
